2609.37743.title: ContextRender: From Execution Dependencies to Agent Context
2609.37743.paper_summary: LLM agents performing long-horizon tasks accumulate tool results that later steps may need. Passing the full history to every invocation is costly even when it fits within the context window, while reducing it risks omitting needed information. Existing context management methods can overlook how earlier tool results are used in subsequent execution, leaving needed information out of context. We introduce ContextRender, which manages context through a persistent graph of execution dependencies. We develop Tool-Flow Analysis to track how later operations reuse information from earlier tool results, providing a signal called observed reuse. A renderer combines this signal with recency and semantic relevance to select results within a fixed history budget, retaining omitted results for later use. Across AppWorld and 8-objective QA with three execution models, ContextRender outperforms the evaluated context management baselines using a 6K history budget, well below the models' maximum context windows. Within this budget, it achieves task performance close to or above that of passing the full history while reducing mean inference cost by 10.2%-32.2% relative to Full history. Ablations show that observed reuse improves task performance and retention of results reused later.
2609.37743.paper_summary_zh: LLM代理執行長期任務時，會累積後續步驟可能需要的工具結果。即使完整歷史符合上下文窗口，將其傳遞給每次調用的成本也很高，而減少歷史則有風險省略所需的信息。現有的上下文管理方法可能忽視早期工具結果在隨後執行中的使用，導致所需信息脫離上下文。我們引入ContextRender，通過持久的執行依賴圖來管理上下文。我們開發了工具流分析，以追蹤後續操作如何重用早期工具結果的信息，提供一種信號稱為觀察到的重用。渲染器將此信號與近期性和語義相關性結合，以在固定的歷史預算內選擇結果，並保留省略的結果以便後續使用。在AppWorld和三種執行模型的8目標問答中，ContextRender在使用6K歷史預算的情況下，超越了評估的上下文管理基準，這遠低於模型的最大上下文窗口。在這個預算內，它的任務表現接近或超過傳遞完整歷史的情況，同時將平均推理成本相對於完整歷史降低了10.2%-32.2%。消融實驗顯示，觀察到的重用提高了任務表現和後續重用結果的保留。
